novel_features.name: Cross-surface FTS search with snippet and switch
novel_features.description: Search workspace titles, surface titles, notification bodies, and sampled pane content with FTS5 — get the surface and snippet, not just the workspace; --switch jumps cmux to the matching surface.
novel_features.rationale: cmux find-window returns workspace-only with no snippet; only a persisted FTS index over titles + bodies + sampled pane text can return surface granularity and surface-context snippet for one query.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent or user knows a phrase but not which workspace, this returns the exact surface to focus instead of forcing a workspace-only walk.

novel_features.name: Notify-driven event stream
novel_features.description: Long-running stream of cmux notification events as JSONL, with pluggable sinks (stdout, file, exec hook, Slack webhook, generic webhook). Replaces capture-pane polling with id-cursored notification events or fsnotify on the session JSON.
novel_features.rationale: ecosystem-manager polls every pane via capture-pane each tick because cmux has no first-class event stream from the CLI; cursored list-notifications and fsnotify on the session JSON close that loop.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets a manager subagent wait on events instead of burning context on full pane scans.

novel_features.name: Agent-status timeline
novel_features.description: Time-series of agent state per workspace (and key) over a window, drawn from local status snapshots persisted on every sync.
novel_features.rationale: cmux carries only the current statusEntry; the historical sequence lives entirely in our store, populated by sync.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers 'when did Tuck go awaiting?' which is needed to triage stuck panes and to bound sync cadence.

novel_features.name: Stuck-pane triage
novel_features.description: List every (workspace, key) whose latest persisted state is awaiting input and whose transition timestamp is older than a threshold.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the local time-series; the live RPC cannot answer 'how long has it been Needs-input'.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surfaces the panes a manager subagent should triage first, without re-capturing screens.

novel_features.name: Normalized agent-state column
novel_features.description: Single canonical state per workspace (idle / working / awaiting / stranded) computed by joining status entries with title-icon decode and surface health.
novel_features.rationale: Replaces three signals (statusEntry value, title icon, surface in_window) with one column; the icon-priority rule from the cookbook becomes callable.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Gives an agent a single boolean to drive 'should I look here?' instead of decoding folklore icons.

novel_features.name: State-transition alerts
novel_features.description: Declarative rules that fire when a workspace transitions into a state (e.g. Tuck claude_code Running -> Needs input). Sinks: stdout, file, exec, macOS osascript, Slack webhook, generic webhook.
novel_features.rationale: cmux notify lands in cmux's own sidebar; rules + external sinks live entirely outside cmux but require our local diff over snapshots to detect transitions.
novel_features.example: cmux-pp-cli alert add --workspace Tuck --on awaiting --sink slack:https://hooks.slack.com/services/X --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: Closes the loop on the user instead of on cmux's sidebar.

novel_features.name: Recently-flipped workspaces
novel_features.description: List workspaces (and keys) whose persisted state changed within a time window, with prev_value and new_value.
novel_features.rationale: Local SQL over status_snapshots; cmux exposes only current state.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Direct replacement for the manager's 'did anything change since my last tick?' question, without rewalking every pane.

novel_features.name: Per-workspace summary card
novel_features.description: One-shot summary for a workspace: metadata (cwd, git_branch, pr) + current status entries + last 3 notifications + last sampled pane snippets per surface.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-entity local join (workspaces + status_entries + notifications + pane_content_samples); cmux requires N RPC calls.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Gives a manager subagent the full picture of a workspace in one tool call.

narrative.headline: Every cmux feature, plus persisted state, cross-surface search, and a notify-driven event stream no other cmux tool offers.
narrative.value_prop: This CLI wraps the cmux Unix-socket CLI with an AI-agent-shaped surface: a local SQLite store of workspaces, surfaces, status entries, and notifications; FTS5 search across titles and sampled pane content with surface-level matches; and a long-running `watch` command that emits cmux notification events as JSONL to stdout, files, Slack, or any webhook so ecosystem-manager-style agents can wait on events instead of polling.
narrative.auth_narrative: cmux uses a local Unix socket at /tmp/cmux.sock with password auth resolved in this order: --password flag, CMUX_SOCKET_PASSWORD env, then the password saved in cmux's keychain entry. cmux-pp-cli shells out to the cmux binary; if cmux is not running or the socket password is wrong, `cmux-pp-cli doctor` says so up front.

quickstart.comment: verify the cmux binary is on PATH, cmux is running, the socket answers ping, and credentials resolve
snapshot every workspace, surface, status entry, and unread notification into the local SQLite store
list every workspace whose canonical state is awaiting input
find which surface mentioned the phrase, not just which workspace
stream notification events as JSONL — pipe to jq, exec hook, or Slack webhook

troubleshoots.fix: install cmux.app and add `/Applications/cmux.app/Contents/Resources/bin` to PATH, or set CMUX_BIN to the binary path.
start cmux.app and wait for the menu-bar icon, then re-run `cmux-pp-cli doctor`.

troubleshoots.symptom: search returns nothing for a phrase you can see on screen
troubleshoots.fix: run `cmux-pp-cli panes sample --workspace W --surface S --scrollback` to seed the FTS table; sync only stores titles + notifications by default.
ensure `~/Library/Application Support/cmux/session-com.cmuxterm.app.json` exists by interacting with cmux at least once after install; fsnotify cannot watch a non-existent path.

troubleshoots.symptom: alerts to Slack do not fire
troubleshoots.fix: test the webhook with `cmux-pp-cli alert send-test --sink slack:<url>`; webhook URLs that 4xx will be quoted in `--json` output.

narrative.when_to_use: Use cmux-pp-cli when an agent or human needs the state across many cmux workspaces in one query, when search must return the surface (not just the workspace) that matched, or when a manager-style loop wants to be notified by event rather than poll every pane. Read-only commands are safe to run while cmux is in active use; write-side actions (focus, send) are gated by explicit flags.

recipes.title: Bulk awaiting triage
recipes.explanation: List every workspace with a normalized `awaiting` state, with the last transition time so a manager can pick the oldest one to look at first.

recipes.title: Stuck > 30 minutes
recipes.explanation: Returns each (workspace, key) whose latest persisted state is awaiting input older than 30 minutes — the exact list ecosystem-manager wants for triage.

recipes.title: Find the surface mentioning a phrase, jump to it
recipes.explanation: FTS over titles + notifications + sampled pane content; with `--switch`, calls cmux `surface.focus` on the top match so you land directly on the right tab.

recipes.title: Replace polling with a notify-driven loop
recipes.explanation: Streams every new cmux notification (id-cursored) and pipes the JSON envelope to the user's handler — the closed-loop replacement for capture-pane polling.

recipes.title: Time-series of a single workspace
recipes.explanation: Drills into a workspace's recent transitions to answer 'when did this start awaiting?' without re-reading the screen.

trigger_phrases: which cmux workspace is awaiting input
